route: O-1 nonimmigrant (extraordinary ability in the arts or extraordinary achievement in motion picture or television), on Form I-129

permit.applies: The US employer or agent (the petitioner) files Form I-129 with USCIS; the performer then applies for the O visa at a consulate
permit.first: An approved I-129 petition, with a written advisory opinion (consultation) from a peer group or labor organization

fees.what: Form I-129 petition, O worker, 1 to 25 named beneficiaries (half for small employers and nonprofits)
Asylum Program Fee on each I-129 ($300 small employer, none for nonprofits)
O category nonimmigrant visa application (MRV) fee

permit.union: Consultation with a peer group, labor and/or management organization is mandatory before an O-1 petition is approved; for motion picture or television, with a labor and a management organization; the opinion is advisory, not binding.
permit.eligibility: "Extraordinary ability in the field of arts means distinction"; in motion pictures or television, "a very high level of accomplishment ... recognized as outstanding, notable, or leading".

sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 214.2(o) Aliens of extraordinary ability or achievement
sources.said: Extraordinary ability in the field of arts means distinction. Distinction means a high level of achievement in the field of arts evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition substantially above that ordinarily encountered … Extraordinary achievement with respect to motion picture and television productions, as commonly defined in the industry, means a very high level of accomplishment in the motion picture or television industry evidenced by a degree of skill and recognition significantly above that ordinarily encountered to the extent that the person is recognized as outstanding, notable, or leading in the motion picture or television field. … peer group (which could include a person or persons with expertise in the field), labor and/or management organization regarding the nature of the work to be done and the alien's qualifications is mandatory before a petition for an O-1 or O-2 classification can be approved. … consultation with a labor organization and a management organization in the area of the alien's ability is required. … Consultations are advisory and are not binding on the Service. … period of time determined by the Director to be necessary to accomplish the event or activity, not to exceed 3 years. … increments of up to 1 year for an O-1 or O-2 beneficiary to continue or complete the same event or activity for which he or she was admitted

sources.title: eCFR, 8 CFR 106.2 Fees
sources.said: Petition for O Nonimmigrant Worker with 1 to 25 named beneficiaries: $1,055. … For small employers and nonprofits as defined in § 106.1(f) , the fees in paragraphs (a)(3)(ii) , (a)(3)(iv) , (a)(3)(vi) , (a)(3)(vii) , and (a)(3)(viii) of this section will be one-half the amount … Asylum Program Fee. In addition to the fees required by § 106.2(a)(3) , (a)(4) and (a)(11) , to fund the asylum program, the Asylum Program Fee must be paid by any petitioner filing a Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker, Form I-129 … $600. For petitions: ( i ) Filed by a nonprofit as defined in § 106.1(f) : No fee. ( ii ) Filed by a small employer as defined in § 106.1(f) : $300.
